title: Who Pulls It In? F = mv²/r Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A stone whirls on a string, the Moon circles the Earth, a car takes a bend. All three go round, so what keeps pulling each one in? And why do Aarav's bicycle tyres slide out when he takes the college gate turn too fast? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn centripetal force.

A live stone on a string goes round a smooth table while an orange tension arrow points to the centre. Double the speed and the pull jumps from 2 N to 8 N, and the graph of T against v bends into a curve. A slow-mo replay cuts the string: the stone carries straight on along the tangent, not outward. We build F = mv²/r = mω²r step by step from Newton's second law, see that it is not a new force but a job done by tension, friction, gravity or a normal force, and derive the top speed on a flat curve, v = √(μrg), where the mass cancels. A car on a flat curve shows friction running out, link by link. Then a worked example on Aarav's bike, the exam trap of counting the centripetal force twice, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:

3:44 Worked example: Aarav's bike on a flat turn
